formLanguage: planar profile extruded along the view axis

objectClass.notes: Vector logotype, not a photographed object. Measured from the source PNG: 99.2% of opaque pixels are exactly two colours (#000000 ink, 40.63% of frame; #e48e00 accent, 0.86%); the remainder is anti-aliasing. There is no shading, gradient, grain or wear anywhere in the reference, so albedo is the only observable channel and every surface response below is inference about a physical extruded badge, not measurement of the reference.

reasoning: Two opaque colour regions only; connected-component labelling of the alpha mask gives exactly two ink islands (18485 px 'J', 17905 px 'C') that touch diagonally, plus one 749 px accent island.
Every edge is a straight segment or a circular-arc terminal in one plane: the whole subject is a 2D profile with depth, so silhouette complexity is high but volumetric complexity is near zero.
No occlusion: the reference is an orthographic-equivalent flat elevation, so nothing is hidden except the side walls and back face that extrusion itself defines.
Held at 'simple' because component count, hierarchy depth and material layer count are all minimal; the detail that matters is boundary placement, which is carried by the traced profiles.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed structure is two macro solids. Meso/micro levels would be invented, not observed: the hairline slits and rounded counter are boundary features OF the letters profile, not separate parts, so they are authored as localFeatures on the letters component and as vertices in its traced contour.

detailInventory.note: Zones scanned with forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py (component-zones: letters-stem, chevron, letters-top-arm, c-bowl-left). Every detail below is linked to a component localFeature or a material localOverride.

details.description: Three vertical transparent hairlines cut through the ink at x=158-161 px (4 px wide, y 0-70), x=171-174 px (4 px, y 0-70 and y 140-209) and x=188-191 px (3 px, full height). They are what separates the J stem from the C bowl; losing them merges the two letterforms into one slab.
details.measurement: slit widths 2-4 px at 417 px reference width = 0.010-0.019 model units

details.description: The J counter is a vertical slot with semicircular terminals, open to the background on both flanks between y=70 and y=140 px. Its rounded ends (radius ~12 px) are the single most identity-defining curve in an otherwise orthogonal mark.
details.measurement: slot x 118-142 px, y 30-180 px; terminal radius ~12 px = 0.057 model units

details.description: The C opens to the right: its upper and lower terminals are cut back on a near-vertical shear, leaving a right-facing aperture. The bowl interior is a stadium-shaped negative space, not a circle.
details.measurement: aperture spans y 0-30 px and y 175-209 px on the right flank of the C

details.description: The accent is a downward-pointing chevron with a concave notch in its top edge and a blunt apex; it reads as a check/tick rather than a triangle.
details.measurement: 48 x 27 px bounding box at x 68-115, y 106-132 px

details.description: Inferred, not observed: on a physical extruded badge the side walls catch the key light at a different angle to the front cap, so the profile boundary reads as a thin lighter/darker rim. Carried as a material localOverride on the side-wall face set.
details.measurement: wall height = extrusion depth 0.12 model units (letters) / 0.05 (chevron)

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Extrusion depth (0.12 unit letters / 0.05 unit chevron) is an authored badge proportion; the single flat reference view cannot supply it.
Side walls are straight, not chamfered, so the front-on silhouette stays identical to the reference.
The chevron is a separate physical piece standing proud of the letter face, per the stated design intent; the reference only shows that it is laterally detached.
Materials are matte-to-satin dielectrics; the reference carries no specular evidence either way.

observations: Flat vector artwork on a transparent background; 417 x 209 px, 5590 bytes, RGBA8.
Exactly two opaque colours carry the mark: #000000 (35413 px) and #e48e00 (749 px).
Reference admission gate: admitted, foregroundCoverage 0.4343, largestComponentFraction 0.9775.
No lighting cues, no shading, no cast shadow, no perspective convergence: the view is equivalent to an orthographic front elevation.
analyze_texture.py: meanLum 0.0, meanSaturation 0.0, gradientStrength 0.0, mottle 0.0, streakRatio 0.0 -- the ink region is perfectly uniform, with zero texture signal.
analyze_texture.py palette #E5930B/#ECAF4B/#F4D29B; the lighter stops are anti-aliasing against the transparent background, not a gradient in the accent itself.
Hairline slits and the rounded top terminal of the J counter are visible here.
Inner wall of the C bowl; straight vertical run with no thickness modulation.

componentTree.name: letters
componentTree.topologyRationale: Decision tree (grimoire/intake/surface_topology.md) step 1: it owns volume, so not material-only. Step 2: not strand-like. Step 3: the silhouette IS the part, not relief on a host. Step 4: YES -- it is a discrete rigid part whose faces are flat and countable (one front cap, one back cap, one straight side wall per profile segment), so assembled-solid is the correct class. It is NOT continuous-sculpt: there is no smoothly-varying volume here, and classifying it so would falsely claim a 3D form that a depth/diagonal ratio of 0.073 cannot deliver. The part is genuinely flat; only the PROFILE is complex, which is why the primitive is 'extrude' rather than 'box'.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Boundary-exact extrusion. The profile is a Douglas-Peucker simplification (epsilon 1.2 px) of the traced alpha-mask contour, verified by re-rasterisation at IoU 0.9917 against the source ink mask (146 false-positive / 159 false-negative pixels out of 36390).

profileProvenance.method: alpha-mask boundary trace on the pixel-corner lattice + Douglas-Peucker
profileProvenance.note: The 'J' and 'C' islands are 4-connected-separate but touch diagonally at image pixel (207,194); they are spliced into one weakly-simple contour through a zero-width bridge at that contact so the pair extrudes as a single solid. Verified with three r186 ExtrudeGeometry: 83 front-cap triangles, cap area 36364 px^2 vs 36390 mask px (99.93%), zero degenerate triangles.

geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: vertex normals from generated geometry; flat caps and straight side walls

collider.notes: Axis-aligned box proxy is exact enough for a flat extruded badge.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: Measured albedo is pure #000000. Authored at #0a0a0c so the front cap does not clamp to absolute black under the badge key light and the extruded side walls stay separable from the cap. secondaryAlbedo is the side-wall value, not a second observed colour.

featureReviews.notes: Front elevation overlays the reference almost exactly. Independent measurement: the traced profile re-rasterises against the source ink mask at IoU 0.9917 (146 false-positive / 159 false-negative pixels of 36390); the pipeline's own coarse-grid gate reads 0.8644 against a 0.85 threshold. Aspect-ratio delta 0.0045, scale delta 0.0045.

All three hairline slits, the rounded J counter terminals and the sheared C terminal aperture survive into the render. The slits read marginally thinner than the reference because Douglas-Peucker at epsilon 1.2 px pulls the 2-4 px slit walls in by up to one pixel; the slit count, placement and full/partial height are correct.

Accent sits in the J counter gap at the measured position and scale (bbox x 68-115, y 106-132 px). Shape IoU 0.9647 against the 749-pixel source mask; the blunt apex and the concave top notch both read. Lower than the letters IoU only because a one-pixel boundary error costs proportionally more on a 749-pixel mark.

Two flat dielectric albedos, no maps, matching the measured two-colour reference. Tier-1 per-component colour delta: deltaE 2.26 and 11.65 against the recipe values. The 11.65 is the accent, and is expected: the authored #e08a00 differs from the measured #e48e00, and the render is tone-mapped while the reference is unlit flat artwork.

Three-quarter view shows real side walls and the chevron visibly standing proud; silhouette area at three-quarter is 1.066x the front area, so the form is not a billboard. Marked down because the ink side walls render nearly indistinguishable from the front cap: the spec's ink/sidewall-response local override is descriptive only, and the generator does not realise per-face-set albedo.

visualEvidence.cameraView: front elevation, orthographic-equivalent, framed identically to the reference (417x209 at 209 px per model unit)
visualEvidence.notes: Capture method is a CPU rasteriser over the real generated THREE geometry (3x supersampled, transparent background to match the reference alpha), not a GPU render of MeshPhysicalMaterial. Specular, clearcoat and image-based lighting are therefore not evaluated.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Side-by-side inspection of comparison-front.png: the J counter slot, all three hairline slits, the C bowl curvature, the sheared C terminals and the accent chevron all land on the reference. performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Already minimal: 444 triangles, 2 draw calls, 0 textures. The only remaining lever is profile vertex count, and reducing it below the current epsilon costs measurable silhouette IoU.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: Not derived from the reference -- the artwork is unlit flat vector, so there is no photographic lighting to recover. Authored upper-left key so the extruded side walls on the right and lower flanks read as depth.
Lifts the shadowed side walls so the front silhouette still matches the flat reference.
Separates the badge from a dark backdrop in the dark theme.

lightingFromPhoto.background: transparent (alpha) -- the host page supplies the backdrop
lightingFromPhoto.notes: ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 keeps the #0a0a0c cap off absolute black without lifting the accent hue.

lightingFromPhoto.strategy: No ground plane; contact shadow behaviour is limited to ambient occlusion across the hairline slits, the J counter and the C bowl.
lightingFromPhoto.notes: The badge floats in the hero, so a ground shadow would be fabricated. Contact darkening is handled by the counter-cavity-ao local override on the ink material.

proceduralStrategy: THREE.Shape + ExtrudeGeometry with bevelEnabled:false and steps:1 -- the only construction that keeps the traced silhouette exact.
Profiles are authored as absolute model-unit vertex lists and the component transform.scale is pinned to [1,1,1], so the generator's dimension-scaling path cannot distort the letterforms.
No textures, no canvas-generated maps, no external art: two flat dielectric materials only.
Deterministic by construction -- there is no procedural noise anywhere, so no seed is required.
Chevron depth and z-offset are the only authored (unobservable) numbers; both are declared in preSpecAssessment.unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation.
Triangle count is fixed at 444 (letters 344 + chevron 100), measured with three r186.

animationAnchors.notes: Pointer-parallax yaw/pitch of the whole badge about its centre.
Independent z push of the accent for a depth cue on hover.
Ink albedo swaps between #0a0a0c (light theme) and a near-white value (dark theme).

destructionAnchors.notes: Logotype integrity is the point of the asset; never fracture.
Detachable as a whole for transitions, but not fracturable.

risks.description: Extrusion depth and side-wall treatment are authored, not measured. A different depth changes the three-quarter read but not the front elevation.
risks.mitigation: Depth lives in one spec field per component; Task 3 can retune without retracing.

risks.description: The three hairline slits are 0.010-0.019 unit wide. Below roughly 120 px of on-screen badge height they fall under one pixel and alias.
risks.mitigation: Render with antialias:true and pixelRatio >= 2; do not thin them further.

risks.description: The letters profile is weakly simple: it passes through the J/C diagonal contact twice via a zero-width bridge. A tessellator less robust than earcut could emit a sliver there.
risks.mitigation: Verified with the project's own three r186: 83 cap triangles, zero degenerate, cap area within 0.07% of the mask. Re-verify if the three version changes.

risks.description: No browser/WebGL capture was available in this environment, so the pipeline's AI-vision pass gate could not be closed on a real GPU render.
risks.mitigation: Deterministic CPU rasterisation of the generated geometry was used for the review sheets; a browser capture is still owed before the pass is claimed locked.
